responsibility: This module is GCC’s target backend for the LoongArch architecture, covering target option resolution, ISA and ABI selection, native CPU detection, RTL instruction selection, scheduling, assembly emission, and operating-system integration for LoongArch-based systems. Its core backend files define machine properties, calling convention and code-generation hooks, while the main machine descriptions, predicates, constraints, and sync support map GCC RTL onto scalar, atomic, and synchronization instructions; SIMD support is split into shared vector infrastructure plus LSX and LASX pattern files and user intrinsic headers. The module also contains builtin and frontend-facing target interfaces, including C-family and D predefined macros, target attributes, and LoongArch-specific builtin expansion, along with centralized tables for CPU types, tuning costs, ISA-evolution metadata, and option strings that drive -march/-mtune/-mabi/-mfpu handling in both the compiler and driver. Platform headers for ELF, Linux, GNU userlands, and musl/bare-metal environments provide linker/spec defaults, while generic and core-specific scheduler models such as the generic and LA464 descriptions distinguish microarchitectural tuning within the overall LoongArch backend.
